risk_assessment.rationale: The invoice contains a classic bank-detail-change notice directing payment to a new account for this and all future payments. No other manipulation language is present, but this unverified change is a high-risk fraud pattern requiring verification.

signals.explanation: Invoice instructs recipient to abandon prior bank details and use a new account for this and all future payments, a common invoice fraud / bank-detail-change scam pattern.
signals.quote: Please note: our bank details have changed.

skeptic.argument: The invoice is internally coherent: quantities, unit prices, subtotal GBP 529.00, 20% VAT and total GBP 634.80 for receipt paper and kraft bakery bags plausibly supplied to Ashgrove Bakery, with invoice and due dates 30 days apart and no urgency pressure. The beneficiary name matches the supplier name, Fennimore Stationery Ltd, as given at the top of the document, and a bank-detail change alone is also consistent with a legitimate supplier moving banks and notifying customers on an official invoice. On the facts in the item there is no mismatched name, inflated total, or executive-domain impersonation of the recipient ashgrovebakery.example to establish fraud.
skeptic.evidence_that_would_change_my_mind: Call Fennimore Stationery on a phone number already on file (not from this invoice) and ask them to confirm invoice FS-2026-1190 and that IBAN GB03 ZZTB 6091 7233 0198 44 is their new account; if they deny it or have no record, treat it as fraud.
